risks.description: A view billed as read-only silently performs a write (creates an effect grant, a claim row, or POSTs to the TMS) — the single most consequential failure for a write-fencing freight teammate.
risks.basis: AC 'the view performs no write of any kind' (weight 3, PENDING); effect_grants is the canonical single-commitment ledger per schema.py.

risks.description: Malformed or hostile search input (SQL metacharacters, over-long strings) crashes the endpoint (500) or, worse, injects into the read query and mutates state.
risks.basis: AC3 read-only invariant plus general query-construction risk on a new user-facing search surface.

risks.description: Adding the view regresses existing write-fence / tenant-first invariants that the canonical suite guards.
risks.basis: U-RO-3 adds a new surface into a codebase whose identity is a governed write fence; full canonical suite is the guard.

risks.description: The view leaks another tenant's shipments, since every canonical table is tenant-first but the AC set is silent on scoping for this new read surface.
risks.basis: schema.py enforces tenant-first PKs everywhere; the U-RO-3 AC set does not name tenant scoping — a gap, not a promise.

assumptions: The read-only shipment view is served by the loopback app at http://127.0.0.1:8001 as an HTTP GET surface (the prompt provisions a loopback app URL specifically for request paths); its exact route is assumed to be /shipments with a `reference` query parameter.

The app on 8001 is backed by data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 (the only approved sqlite3 target), and that DB has the canonical schema created at startup so effect_grants / operation_action_claims / delivery_action_claims exist and start empty for the run.
Shipment/load reference '560003' is seeded and resolvable (it recurs as a load/search reference across eval/tests/test_operator_agent.py); 'ZZ-NO-SUCH-REF-9999' resolves to nothing.
'No write of any kind' is verified as zero rows in the canonical write-commitment tables (effect_grants and the action-claim tables); read-only telemetry, if any, is not treated as a business write.
unresolved_questions: What is the actual surface and route of the read-only view (HTTP path + param names, CLI, or Slack read)? I could not locate an implementation of U-RO-3 in src/; every request-based scenario assumes GET /shipments?reference= and will spuriously fail if the real contract differs.

What exact text does the view emit for a no-match search? AC2 requires it to 'say so', but I could not find the copy string, so S3 can only assert 200-with-no-error, not the presence of the specific 'no shipments matched' message. Provide the literal string to strengthen the oracle.
What are the real seeded shipment references and their fields in the run's dataset? Without them the happy-path echo assertion (S2) is a guess ('560003').

Is the search meant to read the workflow DB, the mock TMS, or both? If shipments live in the mock TMS, a 'no write' check must also confirm no TMS mutation, which no approved command can currently inspect.

Should this view be tenant-scoped? Every canonical table is tenant-first, but the U-RO-3 AC set is silent on cross-tenant read isolation — this looks like a real gap (R6) that should be an explicit acceptance criterion rather than left inferred.
